terra.problem: “Jacob sends word to Esau” describes Jacob sending the messengers and becoming afraid, but those events are not said to happen in Seir. The messengers went to Esau there.
“Esau settles in Seir” attributes the lack of room to Esau and his family’s possessions. Genesis 36:7 says the possessions of Esau and Jacob were too great for them to dwell together.
“Israel passes by Seir” says Israel paid for food and water, but Deuteronomy 2:1–8 records God’s instruction to pay, not that they did so.

“God defeats the armies” involves men from Mount Seir, but the battle is not said to happen there. Also, “the people of Mount Seir” could suggest that all its inhabitants were destroyed, rather than the men in the invading army.
